summary: One surface colour. Depth comes from a light shadow and a dark one, and nothing else.
source: neumorphism.io (canonical CSS) · dev.to §2/§6 · 2026 practice: Big Human, Setproduct, Clay, mycodelesswebsite
researchNote: Checked against 2026 write-ups before building. Two things changed the design: (1) the style has moved toward a CLAYMORPHIC hybrid - softer, more tactile, less extreme shadow; (2) its real home is the SINGLE-PURPOSE INSTRUMENT - music player, smart-home control, calculator, health tracker - 'where the whole screen is one calm instrument'. It is not a marketing-page style, and building it as one is the commonest way it looks wrong. Modern practice also applies it SELECTIVELY and at higher contrast than the 2020 original, because early neumorphism routinely failed WCAG.

surface.role: ONE colour, mid-light. Figure and ground are identical - that is the whole illusion

ink.role: desaturated slate. Darkened from the classic #4b5162 to clear 4.5:1 - early neumorphism failed this routinely

muted.role: secondary text, still 4.5:1 on the surface

accent.role: colour lives in an ICON or in TEXT, never in the plate. Darkened from #4a5cf0, which is 4.16:1 on the surface and fails body text

radius.note: 2026 practice softened this: the classic 50px reads as a blob at instrument scale. 16/32 is the claymorphic range.

shadow.rule: BOTH shadows, always. One alone is a drop shadow, not an extrusion.

border.note: none. A border kills the extrusion - it draws an edge the light was supposed to imply.

focus.reason: the extrusion cannot carry focus - a raised control and a focused raised control look identical. The ring is the accent, offset far enough to clear the light shadow, and it is the ONE place a hard edge is permitted.

motion.note: raised to pressed, both shadows inverting together. 140ms - soft, because the material is soft.

copyBudget.headlineReason: an instrument has a label, not a headline
copyBudget.note: the second-lowest budget in the catalogue. This is a COMPONENT style: if you are writing paragraphs, the page has stopped being an instrument.

a11y.contrastProblem: This is the pack with the most accessibility debt in the catalogue, and 2026 sources say so directly: early neumorphism routinely failed WCAG. The extrusion is made of two LOW-CONTRAST shadows against their own surface - #c3c7cd on #e4e7ee is 1.35:1, nowhere near the 3:1 that 1.4.11 needs for a control boundary.
a11y.resolution: The shadow is decorative, not the affordance of record. Every control must ALSO carry a text label or an icon at 4.5:1, and interactive controls get a 44px target (not 24) because a soft edge is genuinely harder to aim at than a hard one.
a11y.selectiveRule: 2026 practice applies the extrusion SELECTIVELY - to the few controls that are the instrument, not to every surface. A page where everything is extruded has no hierarchy, because extrusion was the only hierarchy signal available.
a11y.radiusNote: Raised to 50 because a dial is border-radius:50% — on a 96px dial that resolves to 48px, which is a control geometry, not a soft-UI decision. The 16/32 rule still governs rectangles.
a11y.accentNote: The classic neumorphic accent #4a5cf0 is 4.16:1 on a #e4e7ee surface — under 4.5:1. Because this pack forbids colour in the plate, the accent is only ever TEXT, so it must clear the body-text bar rather than the 3:1 non-text one. Darkened to #3d4bd1 (6.4:1).

banned: more than one surface colour - the illusion depends on figure and ground being identical
any accent fill on the raised element itself - colour goes in an icon or in text, never in the plate
pure white or pure black surfaces - you lose one of the two shadows
dark neumorphism at low contrast - the light shadow has nowhere to go
text or icons inside a pressed well at body size
extruding every surface on the page - it destroys hierarchy

darkMode.note: The hard case, and the sources agree: on a dark surface the LIGHT shadow has almost nowhere to go. #2a2d35 gives a light shadow of only #343842 - a 1.15:1 lift. Dark neumorphism therefore leans on the dark shadow and accepts a shallower extrusion; it is a real limitation, not a tuning problem.

scroll.headline: scroll-reveal (⚠ — constrained)
scroll.reason: compatibility.md rates reveal ⚠ for this pack, NOT ●, and the constraint is specific: "fine on the components, but note the style's existing a11y debt (no border, no fill contrast, WCAG 1.4.11 unmet). Do not add an opacity:0 start state to a control that is already hard to perceive." This pack has NO ● entry — its own scope is the constraint, because every source describes it as a COMPONENT style and page-scale techniques have nothing to act on.
banned: parallax — ✗ on first principles. One surface colour means figure and ground are identical; layers moving at different rates require layers, and this style has none
scroll-theme-shift — ✗. The dark shadow is surface x 0.87 and the light shadow is surface +13%. Animate the background and both shadows become wrong, so the extrusion inverts or disappears mid-scroll
pinned-scene, scrollytelling — ✗. Page-scale techniques have nothing to act on in a component style
scroll.constrainedForm: Per ROUTER Gate 3.5, a ⚠ is built in its CONSTRAINED form: the reveal animates transform only and starts at opacity 1, never 0. A control whose only affordance is a pair of low-contrast shadows must never begin invisible.

sheet.metaLine: one surface · d=6/12/20 · blur 3xd · both shadows always · no borders
tokenTable: ONE colour. Figure and ground identical
not 24 - a soft edge is harder to aim at

notes.tokens: Four numbers and one colour. Both shadows, always — one alone is a drop shadow, not an extrusion. And the 2026 correction: text darkened from the classic #4b5162 to #2f3542, because early neumorphism routinely failed WCAG and the sources say so directly.
notes.nav: A pressed track holding raised pills. The active item is RECESSED — in a single-surface world, the only two states available are up and down.
notes.hero: Not a hero — an instrument label. Five words maximum. The 2026 sources are explicit that this style's home is the single-purpose screen: a player, a thermostat, a calculator. Build it as a marketing page and it looks wrong immediately.
notes.button: Focus cannot use the extrusion, because a raised control and a focused raised control are identical. The ring is the accent at 4px offset — far enough to clear the light shadow, and the one place a hard edge is permitted.
notes.form: An input is a pressed well. Note the rule the pack states against itself: no text at body size inside a pressed well — the inner shadow crosses the first line of text. Labels sit outside.
notes.card: d=12, blur 36. And the 2026 correction that matters most: extrude selectively. A page where every surface is raised has no hierarchy, because extrusion was the only hierarchy signal there was.
notes.table: The pack's weakest module by a distance. Rows cannot be extruded — 30 raised strips is noise — so the table sits inside one pressed well and uses type alone. Honest answer: if you need a data grid, this is the wrong pack.
notes.overlay: A raised panel over a soft scrim. There is no other elevation available, so the scrim does the separating and the panel simply uses the largest d on the page.
notes.empty: A pressed well with nothing in it. Like skeuomorphism, this pack has a natural vocabulary for absence: an empty socket needs no explanation.
notes.dark: The hard case. On #2a2d35 the light shadow can only reach #343842 — a 1.15:1 lift. Dark neumorphism leans on the dark shadow and accepts a shallower extrusion. That is a real limitation of the technique, not a tuning problem.
notes.narrow: Targets go to 44px, not 24 — a soft edge is genuinely harder to aim at than a hard one, and this is the one pack where the WCAG minimum is not enough.
notes.copy: 220 chars per viewport, the second-lowest here. If you are writing paragraphs, the page has stopped being an instrument.
